requirements.statement: Regional Knowledge Base is intended for routine mass ingestion of books, not isolated successful demos. The system is mass-ingestion-ready only when production-like capacity, retrieval quality, latency, import-quality and operational-reliability gates all pass.
acceptance: The minimum engineering scale benchmark covers at least 100 book-equivalent sources and 100,000 active chunks, or a larger real corpus when available; this is a readiness benchmark, not a product limit.
Routine imports are resumable and idempotent, use bounded queues/backpressure, do not require keeping a ChatGPT turn open, and one failed/superseded revision cannot block unrelated books.
A book is not considered accepted merely because text or vectors were written; its active revision must pass the required import and retrieval acceptance.

Exact accepted inputs, model/human payloads and resolved mutations are remotely durable before final accepted ACK; Saved additionally requires a committed, recoverable exact outcome. Local receipt is pending. Replay preserves IDs, revisions and chosen facts without new model inference; derived projections have separate hashes/readiness. Snapshot-plus-tail restores control state and domain effects after DevCoveer disk loss.

requirements.statement: Mass ingestion must remain within measured working-storage capacity with explicit headroom. The target architecture uses one PostgreSQL/pgvector working corpus in Kaggle and a bounded durable control journal on DevCoveer; this stable requirement ID retains its historical name but does not require Supabase.
acceptance: Full source binaries, scans and BGE weights remain outside the control SQLite database. Account for PostgreSQL heap, vectors, indexes, TOAST, WAL, system overhead, temp files, staged imports, restore/snapshot overlap, and separately bounded control journal, recovery objects and caches.

At the production-like scale benchmark, measured steady-state usage is at most 80% of each applicable storage budget and the largest-source reimport, snapshot/restore and cutover peak is at most 90%; document the actual provider limits and reserved headroom.
Capacity is established from measured database, volume and object-storage usage/growth, not row-count or raw-vector arithmetic alone.
Corpus completeness, evidence provenance and retrieval quality are not silently reduced merely to fit quota; if the gate fails, storage/index representation is optimized and remeasured.

DevCoveer raw spool is bounded to a few hours and a measured byte cap. Verified remote tail separately covers designated recoverable baselines and unfinished consumers. Local GC need not wait for a daily baseline; remote GC must preserve its coverage. UNKNOWN, active requests and dedup receipts do not expire with raw spool. Backpressure precedes loss of unprotected work.

Incremental projections, reference-aware cache/tail GC and measured autovacuum/ANALYZE keep storage bounded. Full reembedding/REINDEX is event- or evidence-driven, not a nightly default. Shadow indexes, Dataset versions, upload/restore overlap and WAL are included in peak capacity; remote snapshot bytes do not pass through the control spool.

requirements.statement: Dense vector retrieval must independently provide high-quality evidence discovery; lexical/FTS retrieval is a bounded complementary signal and must not mask weak vector search.
acceptance: The held-out source-grounded retrieval gate contains at least 30 distinct fact families and reports known-evidence Hit@5, Hit@10 and language slices without using lexical retrieval to prefilter dense candidates.
BGE-only known-evidence Hit@5 is at least 85% and Hit@10 at least 90% on the accepted held-out benchmark.
Every critical language slice that is part of the product, including Russian queries over German sources while German books are in scope, reaches at least 85% known-evidence Hit@10.

Release acceptance always reports BGE-only, lexical-only and configured-fusion ablations separately; one branch cannot hide another branch's degradation. E5 is removed from the target runtime, storage, fallback and required gates; old E5 measurements remain historical evidence only.
Retrieval metrics use source-grounded evidence and held-out fact families and are not mislabeled as generated-answer accuracy.

requirements.statement: Knowledge search must have predictable low latency suitable for repeated agent tool calls, with bounded degradation rather than hidden long waits.
acceptance: On a production-like corpus and representative concurrency, warm backend ranked-candidate retrieval has p95 <= 1000 ms.
Public MCP search has p95 <= 1500 ms and a hard interaction deadline of 2000 ms for the evidence-search path.
No normal retrieval branch introduces an implicit multi-second or 10-second wait; unavailable slow branches either complete inside the same budget or return an explicit degraded state.
Latency acceptance reports percentiles, not only averages or best-case single queries.

Source, story, catalog, entity and GEO retrieval use bounded indexed SQL, keyset pagination and batched hydration, not full-corpus Python scans. Actual prepared plans, ANN filtering/recall, index freshness and maintenance under import/search concurrency are verified at scale; stale or incomplete projections are explicit.

requirements.statement: Each imported book must preserve source fidelity and be chunked for retrieval rather than for page layout or transport convenience.
acceptance: Scanner/service material that is not part of the book is excluded while printed book material and document->page->region provenance are preserved.
Retrieval chunks are coherent semantic passages around the measured approximately 256-token operating target; page boundaries are provenance and are not default embedding boundaries.

The exact final embedding input, including any prefix, is counted with the pinned deployed BGE tokenizer; exceeding its current 512-token hard limit blocks acceptance rather than silently truncating. Increasing this limit requires a measured retrieval/import-quality change gate; an E5 tokenizer is not a target dependency.

Before a newly imported or reprocessed book is considered accepted, source-grounded natural-query retrieval checks run against that exact active revision, including paraphrased queries and cross-language queries when relevant.

Only GEO identities, historical/cartographic layers, geometry/CRS, temporal toponyms and minimal GEO provenance migrate. No old books, chunks, vectors, stories, drafts, expert contributions, cases or other non-GEO content migrate. Books are freshly imported through MCP; activation atomically schedules persisted research for disagreement cases without waiting for expert consensus.

Source-bound factual assertions, exact evidence, people and roles, organizations, event dates and calendar precision, quantitative observations and units, historical toponyms/geography and disagreement candidates are retained even when a fragment yields no narrative story. Import and accepted-source re-extraction share this contract; filtering weak stories must not drop factual knowledge.

Story extraction separates facts, episodes, existing dossiers and variants in one workflow. Sufficient episodes save an actual basic Variant.body and exact default revision during import, normally 2-6 connected sentences with separate bibliography. Facts and explicit context gaps remain when no narrative exists. No invented motives/causality, story quota, mandatory length or second model judge.

Ordinary story get/search/read-export and voice expose the actual saved body or a labelled excerpt/reference, never a synopsis or potential rating as the story. Body/default reference/evidence dependencies/receipt are atomic and read back after retry/restart. Read permission is distinct from publication approval; private author drafts are not promoted to shared text.

A small source-grounded blind comparison of actual saved narratives verifies coherence, title promises, faithful uncertainty and known outcome or honest knowledge boundary. Zero-variant success, unsupported claims, false How/Why explanations and loss of factual knowledge are failures; a coherent story need not have conflict or a known ending.

requirements.statement: Changes that can alter search quality, scale or latency must rerun the relevant mass-ingestion gates before production rollout.
acceptance: Changes to chunking, embedding model/space, vector indexes/search, fusion, lexical query formulation, authorization scope or storage placement rerun the applicable capacity, dense-quality and latency acceptance.
A green unit test suite or vector-readiness count alone is never sufficient evidence of mass-ingestion readiness.
Acceptance results identify the exact corpus/revision/model/search configuration so improvements cannot be inferred from incomparable benchmarks.

requirements.statement: These mass-ingestion, capacity, retrieval-quality and latency requirements are protected product requirements and must not be silently weakened or reinterpreted by implementation work.
acceptance: DevCoveer exposes this manifest automatically to implementation and review tasks.
If an implementation conflicts with a critical requirement, the conflict is surfaced instead of normalized into a weaker target.
Intentional requirement changes use requirements_update with an explicit owner authorization reference.

requirements.statement: Experts use the existing Regional Knowledge Base MCP resource directly from any compatible AI client or through Slack with dot as a replaceable executor. Both paths resolve the same canonical person and enforce current capabilities and applicable publication, case and artifact permissions server-side; no separate expert MCP service, endpoint, corpus or identity registry is required.
acceptance: Personal resource-bound OAuth identifies the actual expert, never an owner invite or a client-supplied actor. Supported clients are verified individually; naming ChatGPT or Grok is not a compatibility result.

Slack resolves the verified provider account to the same existing RKB person UUID. A dedicated executor service uses the same MCP endpoint and a durable request/route/generation-bound authority; it never inherits dot's or the owner's unrelated credentials.

Effective permissions intersect current person capabilities, case/artifact scope and delivery audience; service execution also requires its grant/request fence. Active accepted text/bibliography have no book-owner filter. Illustrations are public. Stripe/page quote scans require owner or verified demo/expert/local_historian with scan_proof_read. Full originals and private drafts retain separate grants; import/admin remain owner-personal.
Concurrent actors, cross-route access, lease/link/grant revocation, delayed results and direct calls to forbidden tools are checked on the server, regardless of catalog visibility.

Acceptance demonstrates direct personal research and Slack-delegated research on the same authorized case/revision, including a real non-owner, denial and revocation; documentation and green component tests alone do not establish live support.

Preserve import, actual story body/edit/search/history/variants, dates/calendar, people/organizations, observations/comparison, historical GEO, disagreement cases/contributions/conclusions and private drafts. GEO-only content migration does not reset infrastructure identities/grants/configuration or authorize copying another product's canonical POI/map catalogue.

Mira in Projects Hub remains the preferred voice client through the existing shared live-interaction and typed RKB adapter. Real delegated identity, progressive research capabilities, durable pending/result/receipt continuation and screen evidence are implemented and verified with more than one real user; a search-only adapter or emulator success is not full integration acceptance.

Artifact class and actual accepted geometry are server-authoritative; caller labels cannot turn page/quote scans into public illustrations. Authorized proof uses purpose-scoped original access without owner impersonation or full-file disclosure. Cache hits, history/receipt replay and delayed/shared-channel delivery recheck current dependencies and audience.

Verified demo/expert/local_historian assignment materializes the existing scan_proof_read policy grant with audit and category revision; demo expiry is inherited. Claimed categories grant nothing. Current grant/scope governs rendering; explicit revocation is not recreated on read and category removal withdraws its policy-derived grant.

requirements.statement: Regional Knowledge Base uses one durable user-request lifecycle across clients, preserving per-dialog context and order, equal-person fairness, measured resource admission and honest arithmetic ETA. Ordinary load queues accepted questions rather than discarding them; imports retain capacity for at least one supported search.
acceptance: Slack and supported direct/Mira clients use the existing request authority and MCP resource. Verified canonical people share fairness across clients; client-supplied actors or dialog IDs cannot bypass access checks.

Accepted requests survive restart and retain a final result/delivery outcome in the original dialog. Later dialog turns use completed prior context and cannot overtake an undelivered or uncertain predecessor; other dialogs continue.

Fair selection and measured stage permits apply atomically to every claim/resume/wake path, including an explicit request ID. Control resources, external Kaggle PostgreSQL/BGE, proof/download and vector dependencies are distinguished; capacity is calibrated and adapts to measured resource increases/decreases. E5 is not a target stage.

Forecasts use measured durations and the actual fair order, not an LLM or invented concurrency limits. ETA at most ten seconds causes no waiting message; longer ETA and material increases have durable coalesced notices only for the person's nearest request. Ready final answers take precedence.

Ordinary capacity waits do not consume outage retry budgets, expire accepted inputs or ask users to resend. Proven external unavailability produces one honest terminal response; unknown provider effects reconcile without blind resend and poison stages remain recoverable.

Import stages cooperate at existing safe durable boundaries and cannot consume the measured search reserve. Required BGE publication, source fidelity, prior active revision and Kaggle-only inference remain protected; no process kill or unsafe transaction pause.

The existing evidence-search deadline and latency/quality gates remain unchanged. Report queue wait and time to final answer separately; do not hide a long HTTP search behind the durable question queue.

Acceptance includes cross-client/dialog fairness, restart and stale-generation boundaries, notification thresholds, real resource calibration/resize and import+search concurrency, actual second-client result/ACK readback and held-out ETA error. A green unit suite or pending response alone does not prove product acceptance.

Kaggle keeps authenticated outbound bidirectional WSS to the existing DevCoveer broker. One queue/request authority, claim IDs, writer fence and hashes govern both directions; final ACK follows remote durability and the corresponding application commit. Reconnect preserves a living loaded worker, stale claims do not kill it, and duplicate sockets cannot add a dispatcher.

Unknown provider effects reconcile before resend and have scoped explicit resolution, including abandoned_no_resend without fake success. A provider outage/UNKNOWN backlog does not consume unrelated import/story-save permits. Expired verifiable request IDs cannot execute as new; same-key/different-payload is a conflict, including after recovery and compaction.
